children.text: Data source: Average DO2i during cross-clamp for CŌRE Procedures during mild hypothermia or normothermic periods.
Period: Most recent 45 days. Trend Comparison made to the prior 45 days (i.e., 46–90 days).
Color: If the most recent 45 day average DO2i has increased (green) or decreased (red) compared to preceding 45 day (day 46–day 90) average.
Data Dictionary terms: common procedures; hypothermia, mild; hypothermia, normothermia; oxygen delivery (DO2i & eDO2i).

Data source: Average Hct change at cardiopulmonary bypass initiation for CŌRE Procedures. This is the last Hct pre-CPB - first Hct during CPB.

Data source: Total Case Count is the total number of non-cancelled cardiac surgical encounters. Cancelled cases, even those cancelled after the patient enters the room, are removed from the case count.
Period: Most recent 45 days. Trend Comparison made to the prior 45 days (i.e., 46–90 days).
Color: If the most recent (days 1–45) case count has increased (green) or decreased (red) compared to preceding (days 46–90) case count.

Data source: All Patient Safety Organization (PSO) Non-Routine Event (NRE) reports with a default sort order by report completion date (descending). Clicking the report number opens the full NRE report findings in a new tab.
Data source: The last 100 cases performed with a default sort order by encounter date. Clicking the date will navigate to additional case details.

Color: If the most recent (days 1–45) CPB Case Count has increased (green) or decreased (red) compared to preceding (days 46–90) case count.

Data source: The number of CŌRE Procedures using cardiopulmonary bypass that develop at least stage 1 AKI as defined by KDIGO serum creatinine criteria at 48 hours post operation divided by the total number of non-redo, non-emergent common procedures using cardiopulmonary bypass.
Period: Most recent 45 days. Trend comparison made to the 45 most recent preceding days (i.e., days 46–90).
Color: If the most recent 45 day AKI rate has increased (green) or decreased (red) compared to preceding 45 day (day 46–day 90) average.
Data Dictionary terms: common procedures; AKI, KDIGO Criteria.

Data source: All cases (CPB and standby) performed during the most recently complete 12-month period. Procedures are coded by perfusion staff at the time of surgery.
Period: Most recently complete 12-month period.
Data Dictionary terms: procedure, CAB; procedure, Valve; procedure, CAB + Valve; procedure, Other.

Data source: This chart shows the hospital’s overall consistency measure compared with the Orrum Average. It is a composite of four consistency measures, specifically for Hemodilution, Oxygen Delivery, Mean Arterial Pressure, and Glucose consistency. Each of these reflects how similar the underlying parameters are across the hospital’s recent CŌRE procedures. More details on the calculations can be found in the FAQs.
Period: Hospital consistency is computed on the last 60 complete CŌRE procedures performed.

Important Note: Hospital consistency does not indicate whether the hospital performs better or worse than the Orrum Average. It is simply a descriptive measure of how consistent parameters are across CŌRE procedures.

Data source: This chart shows the hospital's overall Hemodilution consistency measure compared with the Orrum Average. It combines six parameters, namely the average, nadir and first hematocrit during CPB, as well as last hematocrit in the room, hematocrit change at the start of CPB and the number of minutes during CPB that hematocrit was below 21%. Each consistency measure reflects how similar these parameters are across the hospital's recent CŌRE procedures. More details on the calculations can be found in the FAQs.
Period: Hospital consistency is computed on the last 60 complete CŌRE procedures performed. Orrum consistency is computed on the most recent complete quarter among all participating hospitals.

Important Note: Hospital consistency does not indicate whether the hospital performs better or worse than the Orrum Average. It is simply a descriptive measure of how consistent parameters are across CŌRE procedures.

Data source: The absolute Hct change at cardiopulmonary bypass initiation for the most recent 30 CŌRE Procedures for each perfusionist. Hct change at CPB initiation is the last Hct pre-CPB − first Hct during CPB.
Data Dictionary terms: common procedures; hematocrit, first intraoperative; hematocrit, last intraoperative.
Chart details:
The box section represents the middle 50% of all observations (last 30 cases) (25th percentile to 75th percentile).
The point in the box section (color change) represents the median value of the 30 cases.
The upper whisker shows the maximum non-outlier value (within 75th percentile + 1.5 times the inter-quartile range) observed in the last 30 cases.
The lower whisker shows the minimum non-outlier value (within 25th percentile - 1.5 times the inter-quartile range) observed in the last 30 cases.
Data source: The lowest Hct during cardiopulmonary bypass for CŌRE Procedures by each perfusionist.
Data Dictionary terms: common procedures; hematocrit, lowest CPB.
Chart details: This ridge plot indicates the relative frequency of each individual perfusionist’s lowest Hct value on CPB. Peaks represent more common values.
Data source: The first Hct in the room and the last Hct in the room for most recent 30 CŌRE Procedures by each perfusionist.
Data Dictionary terms: common procedures; hematocrit, first intraoperative; hematocrit, last intraoperative.

Chart details: This violin chart indicates the relative frequency of each individual perfusionist’s first and last intraoperative Hct. The relative frequency plot for the first intraoperative Hct is light blue, and last intraoperative Hct is dark blue. The average values for each variable are represented as a dashed line.
Data source: The average Hct during cardiopulmonary bypass for the most recent 100 CŌRE Procedures performed at this location.
Data Dictionary terms: common procedures; hematocrit, CPB average.
Chart details: This statistical process control chart shows:
Individual average Hct for each of the last consecutive 100 cases (points).
The overall unweighted average of all cases (solid middle line).
Upper and lower control limits set at group average ± two standard deviations (light blue lines).

Data Source: This chart shows the procedure's consistency. It combines four measures, namely the Hemodilution, MAP, Oxygen Delivery, and Glucose consistency for the procedure. Each specific measure indicates how stable that parameter is throughout the procedure, capturing both the presence of outliers and the degree of fluctuation over the selected time period. The overall case measure is a composite of the four measures. More details on the calculations can be found in the FAQs.

Period: The case's procedure consistency is measured on the cross-clamp period for Oxygen Delivery, CPB period for Hemodilution and MAP, and the entire intra-operative period for Glucose. The case measure reflects the consistency of the entire procedure.
Important Note: The consistency measure does not indicate how well the procedure performance was. It is simply a descriptive measure of how consistent parameters are held during the procedure.
